previous_notes.author: Dr. T. Hendriks (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with elevated PSA of 2.9 ng/mL. DRE was normal. Transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy was performed, revealing Gleason 3+4 (ISUP GG2) adenocarcinoma in the left lobe. Discussed active surveillance vs. treatment options. Patient opted for active surveillance. Referred to urology for follow-up.

previous_notes.author: Dr. T. Hendriks (GP)
previous_notes.text: PSA repeated at 3.7 ng/mL. DRE remained normal. Discussed stable disease on surveillance. Patient continues tennis twice weekly. Referred for repeat urological evaluation.

pathology_report:
Biopsy 1 (2023): Histological examination of the prostate tissue reveals adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. The predominant growth pattern is described as poorly formed tubules. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified. Perineural invasion is absent. The tumour is located in the left lobe.

Summary: The biopsy findings have remained stable across timepoints, with no histological progression noted.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): grade group 5.
